Separate finding worth keeping: Davey's altitude prior is uniform 25,000-43,000 ft INDEPENDENT of weight, so it places trajectories above the service ceiling for part of the flight, and the fuel tables are the only thing in the model that notices.

original_text: THE FUEL BOTTLENECK IS 20:41, NOT 19:41 - this changes the next step. In the best-model run tempering holds 18:39 (31.25%) and 19:41 (5.67%) exactly where it put them and lifts 00:11 2.5x (4.60 -> 11.62%), but fuel depresses the UNTEMPERED mid-flight stretch: 20:41 2.50% (from 8.82%, now the tightest epoch in the run and below where 19:41 ever sat after tempering), 21:41 7.63% (from 19.34), 22:41 5.54% (from 12.19), 18:25 13.30% (from 36.24). Mechanism: require_power_until = m0011 discards trajectories whose tanks run dry early, and whether they do is largely decided between 20:41 and 22:41, so that is where the fuel factor concentrates weight variance. TARGETED FIX: temper m2041, m2141, m2241 as well (~1.8x runtime per epoch, already implemented and config-gated). The 2.8M-particle-per-mode run is now the fallback, not the first choice.

original_text: The core's Aircraft::burn_fuel stops burning once fuel_kg reaches 0, but the core keeps propagating powered cruise dynamics. Any terminal-stage child whose takeover falls after the core's own exhaustion has therefore flown powered with empty tanks. The end-of-flight module records this as the latent powered_after_core_exhaustion_s. This is how the 12.7% module-vs-core burn gap shows up inside the stage. At a 00:11 hand-off the cost is seconds; at 22:41 it scales as about 0.145 × time-to-onset (minutes).

original_text: HOW FUEL EXHAUSTION IS ACTUALLY TREATED (measured 13 Oct 2026 from run-i-dive config and impacts, correcting the master prompt which said 'single flame-out event' and 'single-engine phase never modelled'). Core: fuel.tanks=2, fuel.single_engine=true, inop_flow_scale=0.5, hold-taper driftdown 207-227 KCAS / 300-1000 fpm / 7-11 kt per min decel / L/D 20.7, and require_power_until='m0011' with hard_reject=true - so loss of the SECOND engine before 00:11 is excluded by construction while loss of the FIRST is permitted. The hand-off carries real per-trajectory fuel state (core request 1 has landed): 711,648 distinct realised flame-out times and no mass at the 00:31:48 that fallback_fuel_kg=2000 would imply. EoF takes over with two tank states (two_tank_takeover=true) and tracks engine count at onset: 56.9% none thrusting, 36.9% exactly one, 6.2% both.

original_text: t_realised_flameout_s IS THE FINAL (SECOND) FLAME-OUT, NOT THE FIRST - the opposite of what the trait doc says. Measured: for the 325,071 rows taking over with no engine running it sits at takeover within a few seconds (median -2.4 s); for the 85,018 taking over with one engine running it is a median 288 s LATER, q95 +1,113 s. So 22.5% of the fuel-exhaustion families fly a real single-engine phase of several minutes inside the EoF stage, and 46.2% of family B begin their descent with one engine running. The first flame-out time is NOT emitted as a column; takeover time proxies for it in the A families but not in B, where takeover is the descent onset.

Any statement about pre-00:11 dual flame-out is therefore excluded by construction, not by evidence.
